content.title: Suns vs. Celtics: Prediction, How to Watch for Free (3/16/26)
content.text: The Phoenix Suns (39–28) visit the Boston Celtics (44–23) today at TD Garden, as both teams look to make late-season pushes to improve their playoff positioning. The Celtics sit four games behind the first-place Detroit Pistons in the Eastern Conference, while the Suns are seventh in the Western Conference — currently in a play-in position but just 1.5 games shy of an automatic playoff spot.The Suns fell on Friday, 122–111, to the Toronto Raptors in a game that Phoenix saw slip away late. Phoenix led for most of the game, which saw 12 lead changes, but tilted toward Toronto in the final two minutes. With the game tied at 110-all, the Raptors closed the game with a 12–5 run. Devin Booker and Jalen Green continue to click as a scoring tandem, holding the fort with Dillon Brooks sidelined. Booker is averaging 31.7 PPG over his last six games, while Green has scored 28.8 PPG over his last five. Boston, meanwhile, snapped a two-game losing streak with a 111–100 victory over the Washington Wizards yesterday. It was a controlled win for the Celtics, who led by as much as 30. Boston shot just 26% from downtown, but dominated the interior with 55 rebounds and 54 points in the paint. Neemias Queta led with a 24-point, 10-rebound double-double that included six boards off the offensive glass. Jayson Tatum scored 20 and grabbed 14 boards for a double-double of his own. Jaylen Brown added 16 points. Boston has the edge here with its tighter defense and more balanced offense. But Phoenix can potentially take this one if Booker and Green get help from a third scorer. Prediction: Boston Celtics 118, Phoenix Suns 112 Injury Report Phoenix Suns Mark Williams — Out (Foot) Dillon Brooks — Out (Hand) Boston Celtics Nikola Vucevic — Out (Finger) How to Watch Suns vs. Celtics Tip-off for today’s Suns-Celtics game is set for 7:30 PM Eastern / 5:30 PM Mountain at TD Garden in Boston. The game airs live locally on Arizona’s Family 3TV and NBC Sports Boston. Out-of-market viewers can stream the matchup on NBA League Pass for free on Amazon Prime Video with a 7-day free trial here.
